lesson.title: React useEffect() Hook: Dependencies and Cleanup
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

goalMatch.note: This video covers exactly what you asked for: useEffect on mount (empty array), on state changes (dependencies), and cleanup with the return function.

sources.title: React useEffect() Hook: Dependencies and Cleanup

steps.title: Build a counter component
steps.instructions: Create a Vite React project and src/MyComponent.jsx (imported in App) with useState/useEffect imported and a count state starting at 0. Render `Count: {count}` and an Add button whose handler calls setCount(c => c + 1).

targets.caption: count state starts at 0
Handler adds one using previous state
Rendered count paragraph and Add button

explanations.topic: Importing useEffect alongside useState from React
Creating a count state variable with a setter, initial value 0
Using an updater function with the previous state to add one

hints: Import both hooks in one line: import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'.
Declare state with array destructuring: const [count, setCount] = useState(0).

Render

Count: {count}

and a
Inside addCount, call setCount(c => c + 1) so it uses the previous state.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={addCount()} which calls the function during render and causes an infinite re-render loop.
Forgetting to import and render MyComponent inside App.jsx, so nothing shows in the browser.
Forgetting to export MyComponent as default.
Returning two sibling elements without wrapping them in a fragment <> </>.
Using setCount(count++) which mutates a const and throws an error.

steps.title: Update title on every render
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx call useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }) with no dependency array. Click Add and confirm the browser tab title updates on each render.

targets.caption: Effect with no dependency array runs after every render
Side effect: update the browser tab title

explanations.topic: useEffect runs side code every time the component re-renders
Place useEffect near the top of the component
useEffect takes a function and an optional dependency array
Omitting the dependency array means run after every render
Effect also runs initially on mount

hints: Import useEffect from 'react' alongside useState.
Call useEffect near the top of your component, after your useState line, passing an arrow function.
Inside the arrow function, assign document.title a template string that includes count.
Leave out the second argument so the effect runs on every render: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; });
common_mistakes: Forgetting to add useEffect to the import from 'react' (useEffect is not defined).
Passing an empty array [] as a second argument, so the title only updates once on mount.
Using regular quotes instead of backticks, so ${count} appears literally in the title.
Calling useEffect inside the JSX, a handler, or a condition instead of at the top level of the component.
Writing document.title(...) as a function call instead of assigning with =.

steps.title: Run effect only on mount
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx add useEffect setting document.title to the count, with an empty dependency array [] so it runs only on mount.

targets.caption: Add an empty array [] as useEffect's second argument
This title update now runs only once, on mount

explanations.topic: Empty dependency array runs the effect only on mount
Title updates once and never again after pressing add
One-and-done effects like setting a static title
Why skipping the array re-runs the effect every render

hints: useEffect takes a second argument after the callback function.
Pass an empty array of dependencies to run the effect only when the component mounts.
Write it as useEffect(() => { document.title = ... }, []); then press add. The title should stay the same after the first render.
When you're done observing, remove the [] again (revert), as the presenter does before the next step.
common_mistakes: Putting [] inside the callback body instead of as useEffect's second argument.
Forgetting the comma between the arrow function and the [] array.
Expecting the title to update when pressing add, even though with [] it only sets once on mount.
Leaving [] in place when moving on to the next step, which then adds count to the dependency array.

steps.title: Depend on count, add subtract
steps.instructions: Change the dependency array to [count] so the effect reruns when count changes. Add a Subtract button calling subtractCount, which does setCount(c => c - 1).

targets.caption: Dependency array now holds count: runs on mount and whenever count changes
subtractCount uses the previous state minus one
New Subtract button; the tab title updates on add or subtract

explanations.topic: Values in the dependency array: run on mount plus when that value changes
No dependency array runs on every re-render, even unrelated ones
Adding a subtract button to show any change to count triggers the effect

hints: The second argument to useEffect is an array. What value should you put inside it?
Put your count state variable in the array: useEffect(() => {...}, [count]).
Copy your addCount function, rename it subtractCount, and use setCount(c => c - 1).
Add <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button> next to the Add button.
common_mistakes: Leaving the dependency array empty ([]), so the title only updates on mount.
Writing onClick={subtractCount()}, which calls the function during render instead of passing it.
Writing setCount(count - 1) instead of the updater form c => c - 1.
Copying addCount but forgetting to change + to -, or forgetting to rename it.

steps.title: Add color to dependencies
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx add a color state with useState, a Change Color button whose changeColor handler toggles between green and red, and style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}. Include color in document.title and use dependency array [count, color].

targets.caption: New color state variable, starting as green
Toggles color between green and red
Effect now re-runs when count or color changes
Click to flip the count's color and update the title

explanations.topic: Updater function with previous state in a ternary toggle
Inline style needs a JS object, hence double curly braces
Without color in dependencies, title ignores color changes
Effect runs whenever any listed dependency changes

hints: Add a second state variable for color next to count, starting at 'green', and include it in the title template.
Write a changeColor function that calls setColor with an updater: c => c === 'green' ? 'red' : 'green'.
Style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}. The outer braces embed JS and the inner ones make an object.
Change the useEffect dependency array to [count, color] so the title also updates when the color changes.
common_mistakes: Leaving the dependency array as [count], so the title doesn't update when only the color changes.
Writing style={color} or style="color: color" instead of style={{color: color}}.
Using onClick={changeColor()}, which calls the function during render instead of passing it.
Using = instead of === in the ternary comparison.
Forgetting to add ${color} to the document.title template string.

steps.title: Track window size with listener
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx create width/height state from window.innerWidth/innerHeight, render them as `Window width: {width}px` and `Window height: {height}px`, and write handleResize to set both. Temporarily add `window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize)` and a console.log in the component body to see listeners pile up.

targets.caption: width/height state initialized from the window size
handler that updates both state variables
listener added directly in the component body (temporary)
rendered width and height in pixels

explanations.topic: State initialized from window.innerWidth/innerHeight
Displayed size doesn't update without a resize listener
Adding a resize event listener with a callback
Listener in component body is re-added on every render, piling up

hints: You need two useState calls, one for width and one for height, each starting from a property of the window object.
Render two paragraphs: Window width: {width}px and Window height: {height}px.
handleResize takes no parameters and calls setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).
In the component body (not in useEffect yet) call window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize) and console.log('EVENT LISTENER ADDED'), then resize the window and watch the console count climb.
common_mistakes: Lowercase setter names like setheight instead of setHeight (the presenter catches this himself).
Calling handleResize() when passing it to addEventListener instead of passing the function reference.
Forgetting the 'px' unit or the state variable inside curly braces in the JSX.
Expecting the size to update before adding the resize listener.
Thinking the piling-up listeners are a bug in your code: it's the intended demonstration and is fixed in the next step with useEffect.

steps.title: Move listener into mount effect
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx wrap the addEventListener and console.log in useEffect(() => { ... }, []) so only one listener is added on mount. Run npm run dev, resize the window and check the console logs it only once (twice in StrictMode).

targets.caption: Wrap the listener code inside useEffect
Listener now added once, on mount

explanations.topic: Adding the listener only once, when the component mounts
An empty dependency array means the effect runs only on mount
StrictMode runs the effect twice in development (setup, cleanup, setup)

hints: The problem is that addEventListener runs on every render. Which hook lets you control when code runs?
Move both the addEventListener call and the console.log into the body of a useEffect callback.
Pass an empty array [] as useEffect's second argument so the effect runs only on mount.
Resize the window and open DevTools. The log should appear once, or twice if StrictMode is on.
common_mistakes: Leaving off the dependency array entirely. The effect then runs after every render and still adds a listener each time.
Leaving the original addEventListener call outside useEffect as well, so it still runs on every render.
Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react'.
Thinking the double log is a bug. In StrictMode React deliberately runs effects twice in development.
Passing a call such as handleResize() instead of the function reference handleResize to addEventListener.

steps.title: Return a cleanup function
steps.instructions: Inside that effect, return a cleanup `() => { window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize); console.log('EVENT LISTENER REMOVED'); }`. Refresh and check the console shows the StrictMode add/remove/add sequence.

targets.caption: Return a cleanup that removes the same resize listener
StrictMode runs the effect, cleans it up, then runs it again

explanations.topic: Returning a function from useEffect performs cleanup
Cleanup runs before the next re-render or on unmount
Why remove event listeners: avoid unexpected behavior and free resources
StrictMode runs the effect, cleans up immediately, then re-adds once

hints: Inside the same useEffect that adds the resize listener, add a return statement at the end.
The return value must be a function: return () => { ... }.
In that function call window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize) using the exact same handler reference, then console.log a message.
Refresh the page and open DevTools > Console: you should see added, removed, added.
common_mistakes: Returning the result of removeEventListener (return window.removeEventListener(...)) instead of a function, so cleanup runs immediately.
Passing a new inline arrow function to removeEventListener instead of the same handleResize reference, so nothing is removed.
Putting the return in a different useEffect than the one that adds the listener.
Expecting the removed message to be absent: in StrictMode development it appears once after the first mount.

steps.title: Add a second useEffect
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx add another useEffect that sets document.title to the window width and height, with dependency array [width, height]. Resize the window and confirm the tab title updates.

targets.caption: Second useEffect sets the tab title to the window size
Dependency array: re-run when width or height changes

explanations.topic: A component can have more than one useEffect hook
Dependency array [width, height] re-runs the effect when the size changes
Effect runs on mount, so the title shows the size right away

hints: Add a separate useEffect call below the existing one; don't merge it into the resize-listener effect.
Inside it, assign a template string to document.title that includes the width and height state variables.
Pass [width, height] as the second argument so it runs on mount and whenever either changes.
Resize the browser window and watch the tab title, not the page body.
common_mistakes: Using quotes instead of backticks, so ${width} appears literally in the title
Omitting the dependency array (runs every render) or passing [] (title never updates after mount)
Putting the title code inside the cleanup return of the listener effect
Listing only width in the dependency array so height changes are missed
Forgetting to import useEffect or calling it inside a condition
